lunch.name: Croque Monsieur (Ham and Cheese Sandwich)
lunch.description: Classic French lunch - toasted ham and cheese sandwich with mustard and béchamel. Adding egg makes it Croque Madame
instructions: Butter outside of bread slices
On unbuttered side of 2 slices, spread thin layer of Dijon mustard and béchamel
Layer ham and cheese on each
Top with second bread slice, buttered side out
Heat skillet over medium heat
Cook sandwich 3-4 minutes until golden and crispy on both sides
Press gently with spatula - cheese should melt completely
Serve hot with cornichons and mustard
lunch.notes: Medium heat prevents burning outside before cheese melts. Pressing helps cheese distribution
lunch.fun_fact: Croque Monsieur is classic French lunch, adding egg makes it Croque Madame (Mrs. instead of Mr.)
alternatives: Add fried egg to make Croque Madame

lunch.name: Salade Niçoise (French Tuna Salad)
lunch.description: Traditional lunch from Nice - fresh salad with tuna, eggs, vegetables and anchovies. Uses local fresh ingredients
instructions: Arrange lettuce on large plate
Arrange potatoes, beans, tomatoes and olives in sections
Top with tuna chunks and egg wedges
Whisk olive oil, vinegar, mustard, salt and pepper for dressing
Drizzle dressing over salad
Top with anchovy fillets
Serve immediately at room temperature
lunch.notes: Traditional recipe calls for raw tuna, but cooked canned tuna is acceptable substitute
lunch.fun_fact: Salade Niçoise is traditional lunch from Nice, uses fresh local ingredients of Provence
alternatives: Use fresh tuna instead of canned

lunch.name: Ratatouille (French Vegetable Stew)
lunch.description: Provençal vegetable stew from French countryside. Becomes more flavorful after sitting overnight
instructions: Heat olive oil, sauté onion and garlic until soft
Add eggplant and cook 10 minutes, stirring occasionally
Add zucchini, peppers, tomatoes, thyme and bay leaf
Cook over medium heat 20-30 minutes, stirring occasionally
Vegetables should be tender but not mushy
Season with salt and pepper
Garnish with fresh basil
Serve warm or at room temperature with crusty bread
lunch.notes: Ratatouille improves overnight as flavors meld. Can be made ahead and reheated
lunch.fun_fact: Ratatouille is Provençal vegetable dish from French countryside, becomes more flavorful after sitting overnight
alternatives: Top with grilled bread and cheese

dinner.name: French Coq au Vin (Chicken Braised in Red Wine)
dinner.description: Chicken braised in Burgundy wine - French dinner classic
ingredients: 1.5kg chicken, cut into 8 pieces (preferably rooster or dark meat)
300g lardons (French bacon or pork belly), diced
instructions: Optional: marinate chicken in wine with onion and herbs overnight
In heavy pot, cook lardons over medium heat until fat renders; remove with slotted spoon
Pat chicken dry; season with salt and pepper
Brown chicken pieces in bacon fat in batches, 6-8 minutes total; set aside
Add pearl onions to pot; brown 3 minutes; remove
Add carrots, mushrooms; sauté 5 minutes; remove
Add garlic, tomato paste; cook 2 minutes
Add wine, scraping up browned bits; simmer 5 minutes
Return chicken to pot; add stock, bay leaves, thyme, parsley
Bring to gentle boil; cover, reduce heat to low
Simmer 45-60 minutes until chicken tender
Return browned vegetables and lardons to pot
Simmer 15 minutes more
Make beurre manié: mix soft butter and flour into paste; whisk into sauce
Simmer 3-4 minutes until sauce thickens
Taste and adjust salt/pepper
Serve with buttered egg noodles or crusty bread
dinner.notes: Marinating improves flavor but can be skipped
dinner.fun_fact: Julia Child's famous recipe elevated this rustic dish

dinner.name: Beef Bourguignon (Beef Stew in Red Wine)
dinner.description: French braised beef in burgundy wine - Julia Child's masterpiece
ingredients: 1.5kg beef chuck or brisket, cut into 3cm chunks
instructions: Cook lardons in large Dutch oven until fat renders, remove with slotted spoon
Pat beef dry, season with salt and pepper
Brown beef in batches in bacon fat (4 minutes per side), remove
In same pot, cook chunked carrots and onions 5 minutes, remove
Add minced garlic, cook 1 minute
Add tomato paste, cook 2 minutes
Sprinkle flour over vegetables, stir 1 minute
Add red wine, scrape up browned bits
Add beef stock, bay leaves, thyme, rosemary
Return beef and lardons to pot
Bring to boil, then cover and braise in 325°F oven for 2-2.5 hours
Add pearl onions and mushrooms to pot
Continue braising 30-45 minutes
Remove herb sprigs
In small bowl, mix butter and flour into paste (beurre manié)
Whisk into stew to thicken slightly (optional)
Taste and adjust salt and pepper
Serve with egg noodles or crusty bread
dinner.notes: Low and slow cooking is essential. Wine and time create the magic
dinner.fun_fact: Julia Child's recipe made Beef Bourguignon famous to American home cooks
